title: LCLI-727 follow-ups: the by-hand owner/repo qualifier, derived-name edge cases, the padded-memberId test, and the case-probe controls
description:
Follow-ups from LCLI-727 (F11-F16): the original round-1 review plus the delta review of the correction at 0c1d5737; PR opum-ai/lore-cli#588. All non-blocking. EVERY claim below was MEASURED against the reviewed head before filing, so the line numbers and reproduction outputs are facts rather than relays -- and one of the three original items narrowed to a test gap once measured.

=== FROM THE ROUND-1 REVIEW ===

(1) QUALIFIED-BY-HAND ids skip the predicate. qualifyDecisionRef (src/core/decision-ref.ts:49) never runs its repo part through isValidQualifier, so `--decision opum-ai/lore-cli:DEC-9` is stored verbatim -- an owner/repo PATH, where DEC-192 (5) says the qualifier is the repository NAME only. F11 closed that hole at all three arms that PRODUCE a qualifier (`--repo`, the derived remote name, memberId); this is the fourth path to the same field, where the author supplies it whole. Measured:
    qualifyDecisionRef("opum-ai/lore-cli:DEC-9", "lore-cli")  ->  "opum-ai/lore-cli:DEC-9"   STORED
    qualifyDecisionRef("a b:DEC-9", "lore-cli")               ->  REFUSED ("invalid decision id")
  So the residual hole is `/` and `\`; whitespace cannot reach it, because DECISION_REF's repo part is `[^:\s]+`. FIX: check the repo part with isValidQualifier in qualifyDecisionRef and refuse BY NAME. This conforms to DEC-192 (5) -- the docstring's "kept as authored" rule covers a VALID qualified id, not an owner/repo one. PROVE BOTH WAYS: an owner/repo qualified id is refused by name; a valid `lore-cli:DEC-9` is still stored verbatim; and a bare `DEC-9` still takes its qualifier.

(2) DERIVED-NAME EDGE CASES. repositoryNameFromRemoteUrl (src/core/decision-ref.ts:99) yields a nonsense name from two pre-existing shapes, both confirmed at the reviewed head:
    repositoryNameFromRemoteUrl("https://host:8080")   ->  "8080"     (a PORT is not a repository)
    repositoryNameFromRemoteUrl("https://host:8080/")  ->  "8080"
    repositoryNameFromRemoteUrl("x.git.git")           ->  "x.git"    (the strip takes one suffix)
    repositoryNameFromRemoteUrl("git@host:.git")       ->  undefined  (already safe: empty segment)
  Neither was reachable by F11's tests, which exercised only whitespace and the separators. FIX: pin both with tests AND decide the behaviour in the same change -- the recommendation is to refuse BY NAME a derived name that is numeric-only, or one that came from an empty path segment, rather than writing a port or a truncation into a committed document.

(3) A PADDED memberId IS ALREADY REFUSED -- a TEST gap, not a behaviour gap, measured: resolveDecisionQualifier({ memberId: " lore-cli " }) already throws "invalid workspace member id", while the SAME string passed as --repo trims at src/core/decision-ref.ts:116 and is accepted. That asymmetry is deliberate (memberId is configuration, not a flag, so a padded id would store a padded qualifier) and F11's tests cover the memberId arm's separators but not its padding. FIX: one test pinning that a padded memberId is refused, recording WHY it does not trim where --repo does. No production change.

=== FROM THE DELTA REVIEW OF THE CORRECTION (0c1d5737) ===

(a) THE DECISION-ARM CASE-COLLISION TEST SHOULD ALSO PIN THE SIBLING. It asserts the `--decision` arm returns 0 and that `decisions:` gained the entry, but not that the colliding sibling `adr/0001-a` was left ALONE. The guard it skips is about writing a label that Backlog cannot tell apart from the sibling's; proving the skip should also show the sibling's frontmatter untouched (`decisionsOf("0001-a")` still `[]`). Cheap, and it closes the half of the claim the test does not yet make.

(b) A POSITIVE CONTROL AGAINST A SILENT ALL-SKIP. The case-collision tests are the only real proof of that half, and they are gated on a runtime probe -- so a runner change (a case-INSENSITIVE ubuntu image, or a case-sensitive macOS one) could turn the proof into a GREEN SKIP and nobody would see it. FIX: when the environment says this IS the case-sensitive leg (`process.env.CI` set and `process.platform === "linux"`), assert the probe reported TRUE, failing the suite rather than skipping if it did not. The probe must be able to fail, not only to skip.

(c) COSMETIC: the skip marker says the probe "got one entry back". The probe counts `readdirSync(dir).length === 2`, so the faithful wording is "fewer than two entries" -- a filesystem could in principle return zero, and the message should not name a number it never measured.

=== PREMISE CORRECTED, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-DERIVED ===

One premise of the ROUND-1 review was WRONG and shipped as a test: that the case-collision half is "provably not observable through `link`" because `loadBundle` folds case-colliding ids. It does not -- on a case-sensitive filesystem both concepts load -- and the claim was an artifact of the authoring machine's case-insensitive APFS, where writing `0001-a.md` then `0001-A.md` leaves ONE inode. CI run 38553241722 caught it on the ubuntu leg only. The full account and the rule are on LCLI-727: ON THIS MACHINE, A TEST WHOSE FIXTURE DIFFERS ONLY BY CASE PROVES NOTHING UNTIL A CASE-SENSITIVE FILESYSTEM HAS RUN IT. Item (b) above is what stops that class of error recurring silently.
